In 1979 advocate Pushpa Kapila Hingorani read about undertrial prisoners in a Patna jail in a newspaper. She was not their
lawyer. She had no personal stake in their case. But she walked into the Supreme Court and filed a petition on their behalf.
This was Public Interest Litigation. Any citizen could now approach the Supreme Court or a High Court for a
public cause — without being personally affected. The door that was closed to everyone was now open to all.
What if the petition had been different?
